result.title: Detent: Batch-Invariant LLM Serving and RL Rollouts at Near-Stock Speed
result.summary: Reproducible evaluation, verifiable inference and on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) need an LLM engine to give a request the same output bits whichever requests share its batch. Batch-invariant kernels exist, but engines still select each kernel and its parameters from the batch. Two kernels that compute the same sum can round it differently. The engines' deterministic modes remove the choice by keeping one conservative kernel per operator and pay for it in latency. Many fast kernels are batch-invariant by themselves, so it is enough to fix the few batch-dependent values that kernel selection reads. Detent expresses kernel selection as a program that the engine executes. It finds the fewest values in this program that must be fixed and tunes them for the workload before deployment. On multi-GPU deployments of Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen3-30B-A3B in vLLM and SGLang, Detent is batch-invariant. Tuned per load, it serves at 1.04-1.17x the latency per output token of Stock (each engine with its standard settings), against 1.67-10.3x for the deterministic modes. In SGLang it matches the GSM8K accuracy of SGLang's deterministic mode. Detent covers multiple deployment combinations, including multiple engines, GPU generations, tensor-parallel degrees, and dense and MoE models. Seeded RL rollouts of models up to Llama-3.1-70B replay bit for bit under other batches and cache splits. A trainer on Detent's kernels and values matches every rollout logprob bit for bit at 1.03x Stock's rollout time per token. BF16 GRPO then stays stable where Stock's run collapses.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Detent，把 LLM 引擎的 kernel 选择表达为可程序化分析的对象，只固定少数受 batch 影响的取值，以在几乎不损失速度的前提下实现 batch-invariant 的推理与 RL rollout 逐位可复现。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作属于推理服务层的 kernel 选择与数值确定性工程，虽涉及 rollout 可复现性与 GRPO 训练稳定性，但不触及视觉信息保留、latent 状态生成或证据使用，缺乏可迁移到 LVR 的具体方法线索。
